page: Amazon Web Services m5.24xlarge is a large-scale general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. The instance is built on the x86_64 architecture and features a dedicated 48-core Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz. With simultaneous multithreading active at two threads per physical core, the instance provides 96 vCPUs. The CPU subsystem includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a 35 MB shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AVX-512, and AES instructions. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, preserving a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Network throughput reaches a baseline of 25 Gbps. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local instance storage, requiring remote storage configurations such as Amazon EBS.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture oriented toward parallel computational throughput and aggregate memory bandwidth. The multi-core performance metrics are strong, demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 81290.44 and a PassMark CPU score of 55711.77. Parallel compilation tasks also perform well, logging a Clang compilation score of 39480.0. In-memory throughput is notable, with Redis SET performance achieving 74.72 million operations per second and cached small-block memory reads reaching 4502.38 GB/sec. Uncached large-block read operations register 215.46 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded processing represents an architectural tradeoff: stress-ng single-core performance (1377.89), single-threaded gzip compression (23.75 GB/sec), and Geekbench single-core results (1149.0) fall into the lower quartile.

Without hardware acceleration from GPUs, text generation speeds for language models remain limited, as shown by generation benchmarks falling into the lower quartile across smaller models. From a resource perspective, the instance delivers high aggregate computing density across its 96 vCPUs and 384.0 GB of memory, making it efficient for workloads that distribute easily across many threads rather than processes limited by single-thread latency. Given its balanced resource footprint and 25 Gbps network interface, Amazon Web Services m5.24xlarge fits multi-threaded enterprise application backends, large software build pipelines, distributed caching layers, and high-concurrency microservice architectures.
description: Amazon Web Services m5.24xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based virtual server designed for large multi-threaded environments. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, it provides 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs alongside 384.0 GB of DDR4 system memory, reflecting a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory balance. The configuration features 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth but provides no bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark profiles show leading-tier aggregate performance in multi-core metrics, software compilation, and in-memory key-value processing, recording 74.72 million Redis SET operations per second and strong memory bandwidth across large blocks. However, single-core processing scores and per-thread compression fall in the lower quartiles. Amazon Web Services m5.24xlarge is best suited for horizontally scaled microservices, multi-threaded CI/CD compilation pipelines, distributed caching clusters, and high-concurrency enterprise workloads.
